headline: Democrats take Congress, Ottawa tables its budget, and oil swings on the Iran war
summary: The week was dominated by the U.S. midterms, which left Democrats in control of Congress, and by Thursday's federal budget. The Iran war and oil prices stayed in focus, with Trump now threatening further action, while Ontario dealt with a growing deficit and student protests.

top.headline: Carney government's second budget projects $62.3B deficit with $142B in new spending
top.what: A government source says the annual immigration levels update will be part of Thursday's federal budget, which also targets small-business tax complexity.
top.why: In the briefing on 2 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Oil falls on hopes of an Iran breakthrough after limited U.S. strikes
top.what: Brent crude fell more than 6% to about US$105.55 on hopes of a deal, even as U.S. forces struck Iranian radar and missile sites on Qeshm Island.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as Democrats vow to repeal tariffs
top.what: Tariffs on Canadian goods remain while talks continue, and the DNC chair says Democrats would move to end them if they win power.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Democrats win control of both the House and Senate in U.S. midterms
top.what: Major outlets project Democrats won the House and the Senate on Tuesday; Mississippi and Alaska Senate races were still too close to call and some House races remained open.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Ontario's deficit swells to $16.9 billion as tariffs delay balanced budget
top.what: Ontario's fall update projects a record $16.9-billion deficit this year and $36 billion over three years.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Supreme Court rejects Trump bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots
top.what: The justices quickly refused the administration's emergency request to make California set aside ballots it says may belong to noncitizens.
top.why: In the briefing on 3 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Russian bombing of Ukraine aid centre kills at least 26; Dnipro hit
top.what: Officials say at least 26 people died when Russian bombs hit an aid centre in Komyshuvakha, and separate strikes on Dnipro killed two and injured 20.
top.why: In the briefing on 3 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Economy stalls in August, two days after Bank of Canada's hike
top.what: Statistics Canada says the economy was flat in August and probably shrank 0.1% in September, a weak backdrop for the Bank of Canada's first rate increase since 2023.
top.why: In the briefing on 2 of the last 7 days.
